overview: This table gives a few characters the extra animations used with certain attacks.
description: Single unsharded table of parallel-attack animation-name pairs reached from AttackDataTable.Id_ParallelAttack. CP_030, CP_140, CP_160, CP_240 and CN_230 action controllers resolve its rows through DataTableManager->ParallelAttackDataTables to play and stop CharacterAnimation; the serialized CharacterAnimation_Lower companion has no identified runtime reader.

Id.simple: The name that links an attack to its extra animation. Changing it changes which animation pair the game picks.
Id.technical: FName row/import key (export column ID, ImportKeyField Id; C++ Id at +0x8 of the 32-byte FGameDataTableRow_ParallelAttack). Consumers do not read Row->Id: they read AttackRow->Id_ParallelAttack, reject NAME_None in CP_030, CN_230, CP_240 and through the helper's bCheckNone=true in CP_160, while CP_140 passes bCheckNone=false and relies on FindRow not matching NAME_None. Every reader scans DataTableManager->ParallelAttackDataTables in order and takes the first hit; the manager registers only ParallelAttackDataTable (null loaders are skipped), so precedence is currently moot. A hit is cached in the action's ParallelAttackRow pointer for stop/finish and CP_240 logic, and Reset clears it; a miss caches nothing and plays no parallel animation. All 7 exported row keys are unique and their ID values equal the keys.

CharacterAnimation.simple: Chooses the extra animation that plays with certain attacks. Some characters also use it to change how the attack aims.
CharacterAnimation.technical: FName (NameProperty, +0x10), not an asset path. CP_030, CP_140, CP_160, CN_230 and CP_240 call PlayAnimation(Name, -1.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f, true, false): BlendIn -1 keeps the montage's own blend-in, rate 1.0 is normal speed, start is 0.0 s, bStopAllMontages=true stops other active montages and sets CurrentAnimationName, and bFailOnNone=false is passed. FGameCharacterAction forwards to UGameAnimInstance::PlayAnimationAsset, which looks the name up in the per-instance AssetMap filled from CharacterAnimationDataTable Key/Filename pairs for the character's animation set; an unmapped name silently returns 0. FinishAttackEffects calls StopNamedAnimation(cached Row->CharacterAnimation, 0.0f), i.e. a 0 s blend-out. CP_030 reaches the parallel lookup only when it has not taken its early no-shikigami return. CP_240's EnablesAutoAimOffset compares this field to FName("AttackH_01_Order_01") while the row cache is non-null; that result flows through IsAttackLayerSlot64 into TickAimOffset/AutoAimAlpha, and its FilterRequests adds the controller's default move while the cache is set. All 7 exported names resolve to CharacterAnimationDataTable keys (AttackH_01_Order_01 is shared by CP_240 and CN_230 animation groups).

CharacterAnimation_Lower.simple: This lower-body animation name is saved with the extra attack animation. What it changes during actual play is unclear.
CharacterAnimation_Lower.technical: FName (NameProperty, +0x18), present and non-None in all 7 exported rows (for example AttackF_01_OrderL_01 paired with AttackF_01_Order_01). Six of the 7 names also appear as a Key in the exported CharacterAnimationDataTable; AttackH_02_OrderL_01 does not. No C++ read of this exact property exists in the reconstructed Source/ or Plugins/ tree, including every identified ParallelAttack row reader, and no asset/Blueprint reference to it was found in the partial Content text survey. The lower-body label is therefore a data/name observation, not verified playback; do not assume the parallel readers play it. The empty row constructor leaves FNames as NAME_None, but no exported row uses that sentinel.

notes: Lookup and lifetime: AGameDataTableManager::Tick resolves the single loader named ParallelAttackDataTable into ParallelAttackDataTables at +0x640 (GameDataTableManager.cpp:230, GameDataTableManager.h:141); AddLoadedDataTables skips null tables. CP_030/CN_230/CP_240 use an inline FindRow loop, CP_160 calls Action_FindParallelAttackRow with bCheckNone=true, and CP_140 calls it with bCheckNone=false (the helper's bUnknown parameter is unused). All take the first matching table row, cache it only on success, and clear the cache in Reset; stop/finish uses the cached row's name.

Export coverage checked: one ParallelAttackDataTable with RowStruct GameDataTableRow_ParallelAttack, ImportKeyField Id and 7 rows; no numbered shards or locale variants. The five datatables_by_character copies (CP_030, CP_140, CP_160, CP_240, CN_230) are exact subsets of those 7 rows, not extra shards. Across all five AttackDataTable shards, 18 rows carry 14 distinct non-None Id_ParallelAttack values; all 7 exported IDs are referenced, but CP_070_ATTACKD_01_01 and six CP_170 IDs have no row in the supplied export. That is a coverage/reference observation, not proof of missing retail rows, and no reconstructed C++ reader of a ParallelAttack row was found for CP_070/CP_170.

Cross-table animation chain: CharacterAnimation is a Key in the active character's CharacterAnimationSet -> CharacterAnimationDataTable -> AssetMap chain (GamePhase_BattleBase.cpp:755-775), so the same key can resolve to different montages for CP_240 and CN_230. Playing it with bStopAllMontages=true replaces the currently active montages rather than adding an independent overlay; the name 'parallel attack' describes the attack/parallel-row relationship, not an observed additive montage slot.

Consumer conditions and side effects: CP_030 skips the lookup entirely on its early no-shikigami/no-available branch; CP_140 does not explicitly reject NAME_None. CP_240 additionally uses the cached row for EnablesAutoAimOffset and FilterRequests. The attack-action gate HasNextParallelAttack (GameCharacterAction_Attack.cpp:403-415) tests Attack row Id_ParallelAttack for the next set step, not this table's row; bIgnoreParallelAttackGate requests bypass that gate (GameCharacterActionController.cpp:1342).

Defaults and evidence strength: the row constructor is empty, so unserialized FNames default to NAME_None; all 7 exported rows specify all three names. Playback parameters are normalized rate 1.0 and zero start time, negative blend-in leaves the montage's blend-in intact, and the stop uses a 0 s blend-out. Evidence is reconstructed retail-behaviour C++ with retail RVAs plus serialized exports; some consumers are byte-matched while others are BEHAV/EQUIV-certified (for example 0x10c7e00 and 0x110f130), so exact retail instruction flow is not claimed. Content is partial and no retail Blueprint graph, cooked runtime or live game was inspected; Blueprint-only or retail-only readers cannot be excluded.

usages.detail: Registers the sole ParallelAttackDataTable loader into ParallelAttackDataTables (+0x640); null loaded tables are skipped.
CursedEnergyAttack_1 StartAttackHoming returns early when no shikigami is active/available, before the parallel row lookup; otherwise it plays/caches and later stops the row's animation.
NormalAttack_1 resolves Id_ParallelAttack through Action_FindParallelAttackRow(bCheckNone=false), plays CharacterAnimation and caches the row for FinishAttackEffects.
CursedEnergyAttack_1 resolves with bCheckNone=true, plays/caches the row's CharacterAnimation and stops it via the cached row on finish.
CursedEnergyAttack_2 skips None, scans ParallelAttackDataTables for the Attack row's ID and caches the first hit for play/stop.
CursedEnergyAttack_2 compares the cached row's CharacterAnimation to AttackH_01_Order_01 to enable auto-aim offset, besides play/stop.
CP_240 re-reads AttackRow->Id_ParallelAttack per table, skips None, plays the first hit and caches it.
FilterRequests adds the controller's default move while a ParallelAttack row is cached and the Default layer uses the default action.
Indirect gate: HasNextParallelAttack checks the next Attack row's Id_ParallelAttack for non-None; it does not read this table.
PlayAnimation sets CurrentAnimationName when bStopAllMontages is true and forwards the name plus blend/rate/start parameters to the anim instance.
Populates the anim instance AssetMap from CharacterAnimationDataTable Key/Filename pairs, resolving the table's FName to a character-specific montage.
TickAimOffset consumes CP_240's auto-aim result via IsAttackLayerSlot64 and eases CharacterAnim->AutoAimAlpha.
Exported schema and all 7 row values; row keys equal ID and all three FName columns are serialized on every row.
